scientific_goal: Starting from the confirmed stable TCN15 long-horizon joint-energy-score checkpoint, determine how strongly the horizon-20 and horizon-50 score gradients must be weighted to move checkpoint-trimmed deformation energy and POD covariance trace toward 1 without destabilizing the rollout or sacrificing the one-step fit.
scientific_constraints: Use validation repetitions 13 and 14 for every adaptive decision. Keep test repetitions 15 and 16 locked.

Every trained trial must warm-start from a checkpoint in this lineage. Preserve the restoring-only damped-residual TCN15 architecture, rank 20, full constant diffusion, stored 50 Hz high-pass spatial mean, native-lag velocity state, 5 percent trim, seed 0, kernel 3, channels 64 and dilations 1,2,4. Do not add moments, orthogonality, history noise, stability losses, a new score, a new diffusion family or an architectural change.

Keep the joint displacement-velocity energy score fixed at horizons 10,20,50 with normalized horizon weights 0.1,0.35,0.55, position/velocity weights 2/1, eight particles, 10 percent whole-batch sampling and gradients to drift plus diffusion. This study changes the total energy-score coefficient, not its estimator or state definition.

The imported parent used score weight 0.03 and achieved a 50000-step checkpoint-trimmed energy ratio 1.7078, covariance trace ratio 1.8878, covariance relative error 0.9862 and POD mean RMSE 0.1018. The target is energy and covariance trace close to 1; do not call a lower energy-score value successful unless autonomous rollout energy and covariance also move toward 1.

First complete the exact same-parent pair: one additional epoch at weight 0.03 and one epoch at weight 0.1, both at learning rate 3e-5. Attribute an effect to increased score pressure only from their difference, not from comparison with the imported parent alone.

Use one epoch per trial so checkpoint selection cannot hide a worsening long-horizon term behind an NLL-dominated multi-epoch result. Inspect the actual validation h20 and h50 training terms and the fixed-window gradient audit separately.

If weight 0.1 is finite, retains one-step NLL and innovation calibration, improves h20/h50 scores and moves both rollout energy and covariance toward 1 beyond its matched 0.03 control, use it as the next parent. From that exact parent, establish a weight-0.1 continuation control before comparing weight 0.3.

Weight 0.3 is permitted only after the weight-0.1 gate passes. Weight 1.0 is permitted only after a stable weight-0.3 result still moves monotonically toward 1 but remains clearly underpowered; use learning rate 1e-5 for weight 1.0. Never jump directly from 0.03 to 0.3 or 1.0.

Reject escalation if energy or covariance overshoots below 0.8, either ratio moves farther from 1 than the matched lower-weight continuation, any path is nonfinite, peak POD standardized RMS exceeds 10, peak absolute standardized coordinate exceeds 50, validation NLL degrades materially, or the emphasized h20/h50 scores increase.

Screen every candidate on the same 32 validation paths for 5000 steps. Compare checkpoint-trimmed energy, covariance, POD mean, leading modal RMS, spatial mean, PSD, survival, one-step NLL and innovation diagnostics separately. Promote at most one candidate to 50000 steps, only after the useful matched weight comparisons are complete.
At most six training jobs are allowed. Stop if stronger score pressure fails to produce a monotonic rollout response; do not spend the remaining budget by inventing a different loss or architecture.
advisor_guidance: Treat the initial weight-0.03 continuation and weight-0.1 arm as the required matched comparison from the confirmed parent. The prior fixed audit found h20/h50 expected drift-gradient norms 0.0433/0.0872 at coefficient 0.03 versus NLL 26.0157, while the previous long-score stage nevertheless improved the 5000-step energy ratio 1.8382 to 1.6669 and covariance trace 1.9442 to 1.8217 relative to its matched continuation. The new question is dose response. Prefer candidates that jointly reduce distance-to-one for energy and covariance, reduce leading-mode excess, and improve the fixed identical-window h20/h50 scores while leaving NLL and innovations approximately unchanged. After the initial pair, if weight 0.1 passes, first run a one-epoch weight-0.1 continuation from that weight-0.1 checkpoint. Then compare a weight-0.3 trial from the same parent. A coefficient increase without a same-parent lower-weight continuation is not interpretable. If weight 0.3 passes but remains above roughly 1.15 for both energy and covariance, one final weight-1.0 trial at learning rate 1e-5 may be run from the weight-0.3 checkpoint; interpret it against the established monotonic lineage and do not add another objective. The fixed audit uses coefficient 0.1 for every checkpoint; raw per-horizon losses and gradient directions are directly comparable, and expected gradient norms for training coefficients 0.03, 0.3 and 1.0 scale linearly from that audit. Do not promote before all justified coefficient comparisons are complete.

seed_runs.hypothesis: The confirmed stable TCN15 long-score checkpoint is the immutable common parent for the first coefficient-dose comparison.

initial_trials.hypothesis: A same-objective weight-0.03 continuation measures the effect of one additional epoch without increasing long-horizon gradient pressure.
initial_trials.expected_observation: Small ordinary-continuation changes in fixed h20/h50 scores and rollout metrics; this is the matched control for weight 0.1.

initial_trials.hypothesis: Raising the long-horizon score coefficient from 0.03 to 0.1 makes its direction consequential enough to reduce excessive energy and covariance beyond ordinary continuation.
initial_trials.expected_observation: Lower fixed-window h20/h50 scores and a materially larger movement of energy, covariance and leading-mode RMS toward 1 than the weight-0.03 continuation, with finite rollouts and nearly unchanged one-step NLL.
